executive_summary: Malaysia's EV market is at an inflection point with registrations doubling in 2025 (44,813 units, 5.2% TIV penetration) and hitting 9.18% in January 2026. However, structural barriers persist: charging infrastructure at 56% of target, insurance premium misalignment, repair ecosystem immaturity, and fuel subsidies dampening switching urgency. The market is transitioning from CBU-import-driven to CKD-localized production, with Chinese OEMs investing heavily. Insurance industry faces unique challenges: battery cost concentration (30-50% of vehicle value), limited claims data, and evolving repair cost dynamics. Opportunities exist in customer-centric insurance solutions, second-life battery applications, and ecosystem coordination.

consensus_candidates.claim: Malaysia's EV market doubled in 2025 with strong momentum into 2026
consensus_candidates.implication: Market proof established, adoption trajectory clear

consensus_candidates.claim: Charging infrastructure development lags adoption, creating bottleneck
consensus_candidates.implication: Infrastructure investment critical for sustained growth

consensus_candidates.claim: EV insurance requires fundamentally different risk assessment than ICE
consensus_candidates.implication: Actuarial innovation needed, current models inadequate

consensus_candidates.claim: Battery lifecycle management is critical for long-term sustainability
consensus_candidates.implication: Circular economy approach needed, second-life opportunities

consensus_candidates.claim: Malaysia trails ASEAN peers despite similar incentive structures
consensus_candidates.implication: Policy recalibration needed, infrastructure and fuel subsidy reform

conflicts.issue: CBU tax expiry impact on 2026 momentum
conflicts.position_a: Momentum continues, mass-market adoption driven by CKD (Proton e.MAS 5)
conflicts.position_b: Slowdown forecast due to price increases and infrastructure constraints
conflicts.resolution: Data suggests continued growth but at moderated pace; CKD transition mitigates CBU expiry

conflicts.position_b: JPJ data: 5.1% of TIV in 2025 (includes non-MAA members)
conflicts.resolution: JPJ data more comprehensive; actual penetration likely 5-7% accounting for Tesla/Zeekr/XPeng

conflicts.position_b: LFP chemistry: up to 3,500 cycles, 15+ years potential
conflicts.resolution: Both valid; depends on chemistry, usage, and management; 8-10 years conservative for planning

methods_patterns.proxy_usage: China data for claims patterns, ASEAN data for benchmarking

research_gaps: No published Malaysian EV claims frequency/severity data
Repair cost benchmarks by damage type not established
Consumer willingness-to-pay for EV insurance add-ons unknown
Second-life battery economics at scale unvalidated
Cross-border insurance portability for EVs not addressed
Usage-based insurance models for EVs not explored

manuscript_readiness.recommended_focus: Track 3 (Ecosystem Resilience) has strongest evidence base; Track 1 (Pricing) has clearest data gaps
